title: Dimension of an irreducible closed subset from its generic residue field
statement: Let $K$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $C\subseteq |X|$ be a nonempty irreducible closed subset [def-weil-irreducible-components] and let $\eta\in C$ be its generic point, meaning $\overline{\{\eta\}}=C$. Then the topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of $C$ with its subspace topology equals the transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree] of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] of $X$ at $\eta$: $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa_X(\eta)$.

source.place: Tag 0B1C, item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg in Lemma 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (6), applied to the reduced induced closed subscheme C

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to the closed subset $C$ to obtain a reduced closed immersion $i:Y\to X$ whose image is $C$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i$ identifies $|Y|$ homeomorphically with $C$ with its subspace topology. Thus $Y$ is nonempty and irreducible, and hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The inverse image $\eta_Y$ of $\eta$ is a generic point of $Y$: the homeomorphism takes the closure of $\{\eta_Y\}$ to the closure of $\{\eta\}$ in $C$, which is all of $C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension], $\dim Y=\dim C$. In Lean, use the concrete vanishingIdeal subscheme, take the homeomorphism to its range, and use uniqueness of a generic point in the ambient T0 space to identify i(genericPoint Y) with the prescribed eta.

source.place: Tags 01J3, 01J4, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme and definition-reduced-induced-scheme; with Properties Tag 01ON, lemma-characterize-integral, and Topology Tag 0055

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is an immersion, hence locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (2). The structure morphism of $X$ is locally of finite type since it is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Their composite $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Only local finite type is needed here; no assertion of quasi-compactness of an arbitrary open immersion is used.

Use the affine cover in the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and choose a member $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $\eta_Y$. Then $U$ is nonempty and $A$ is a finitely generated $K$-algebra; since $Y$ is integral, $A$ is an integral domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Apply [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] to obtain $\dim U=\dim Y$. The affine identification and [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension] give $\dim U=\dim\operatorname{Spec}A$, and the explicit prime-chain identification in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}A=\dim A$. Thus $\dim C=\dim A$. The proved private helper integral_dimension_trdeg assembles steps 3--5, using IsAffineOpen.algebra_finiteType_of_field, topologicalKrullDim_opens_eq and IsAffineOpen.topologicalKrullDim_eq.

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, proof of (6) referring to (3): reduction to an affine open

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] applied to the integral scheme $Y$ and its nonempty affine open $U$, the generic stalk $F=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ is a field of fractions of $A$ via the germ map $A\to F$. Explicitly, the map $\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to F$, $g/h\mapsto g_{\eta_Y}h_{\eta_Y}^{-1}$, is well-defined and injective by cross multiplication and injectivity of the germ map, and is surjective by the cited fraction description. It respects $K$ because germs of constant sections give the structure map $K\to F$. By [def-weil-residue-field], $\kappa_Y(\eta_Y)=F/(0)$ since $F$ is a field; the map $F/(0)\to F$, $[f]\mapsto f$, is a $K$-field isomorphism. Thus $\kappa_Y(\eta_Y)$ is canonically a fraction field of $A$ with its prescribed $K$-structure. In Lean, use functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen and FractionRing.algEquiv. Give the function field its K-algebra through the affine sections. RingEquiv.ofBijective applied to the residue map identifies the generic stalk with its residue field: the map is injective because its source is a field and surjective by residue_surjective. Compatibility with K follows by Spec.algebraMap_residueFieldIso_inv_assoc, residue_residueFieldMap, germ_res_assoc and Hom.germ_stalkMap_assoc. These identities identify both maps with constants followed by germ followed by residue.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, integral case; Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, stalk formula

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] with ground field $K$, finite type domain $A$, and fraction field $F$ from step 4. It gives $\dim A=\operatorname{trdeg}_K F$, hence $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa_Y(\eta_Y)$.

source.place: Tag 00P0, lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring, first assertion; the algebra lemma explicitly invoked by Varieties 0A21(6)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso], $i$ induces an isomorphism $\kappa_X(\eta)\to\kappa_Y(\eta_Y)$. It respects $K$ because the structure morphism of $Y$ is the composite through $i$. Such an isomorphism preserves algebraic independence: a polynomial over $K$ vanishes on a tuple if and only if it vanishes on its image, by injectivity and $K$-linearity, and the inverse isomorphism gives the reverse correspondence. Thus their transcendence degrees agree by [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Substitution in step 5 proves $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa_X(\eta)$. The Lean algebra equivalence uses Hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap_comp for its commutes field and AlgEquiv.trdeg_eq for invariance of transcendence degree. Substitute the generic-point equality only after the two algebra structures have been compared.
